sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4.32 billion in FY2016 to $34.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].
The path was not smooth: growth ran 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, then revenue fell 3.9% in FY2023 before recovering 13.7% and 34.3% [D258][D314][D370][D426][D483].

The FY2022 step change came from the Xilinx acquisition, which added $2.4 billion of cash and $1.6 billion of short-term investments and lifted Embedded revenue to $4.6 billion from $246 million [P37][P41][S110][S109].
FY2023's decline was a 25% fall in Client revenue on weak PC demand and inventory correction, partly offset by a 17% rise in Embedded [P35].
Data Center revenue reached $16.6 billion in FY2025, 48.0% of the total, and contributed 15.7pp of the 34.3% growth [S98][D692][D694][D483].
That growth was driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs [P13][P15].
Client and Gaming added 19.0pp in FY2025, with Client up 51% on a 31% rise in processor units and a 15% rise in average selling price [D701][P10].
Operating income grew 94.4% against 34.3% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 20.3% [D484][D483][D511].
Diluted EPS rose 165.0% against 164.2% net income growth, as the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [D487][D485][D506].
Gross margin of 49.5% is the window high, against a 44.7% median [F40][D800][D801].
Operating margin of 10.7% sits above the 7.2% window median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 high [F60][D795][D794].
FY2025's 3.3pp operating-margin gain came from cost of revenue (+0.2pp), R&D (+1.7pp) and other lines (+2.6pp), while SG&A cost 1.2pp [D499][D513][D514][D516][D515].
Gross margin rose only 0.2pp because product mix gains were offset by about $440 million of MI308 export-control inventory charges [D498][P14].
Net margin of 12.5% exceeded operating margin by 1.9pp, helped by a $103 million tax benefit from releasing uncertain tax positions and $577 million of other income [F80][D843][P4][P5].
Operating cash flow of $7.71 billion was 1.78x net income, and free cash flow of $6.74 billion was 1.55x, against a 1.17x window median [F110][F70][D470][F130][D471][D810].
Free cash flow margin of 19.4% matches the FY2021 high of 19.6% and is far above the 6.5% median [D467][D803][D804].
Operating cash flow was reduced by a $2.2 billion inventory build to support the Data Center ramp [P3].
Capex of $974 million was 2.8% of revenue and 1.87x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F120][D466][D472].
Net cash reached $6.46 billion, or 18.6% of revenue, with cash and investments of $10.6 billion against $4.10 billion of debt [D476][D477][D474][D475].
That net cash position ranks at the 100th percentile of five semis peers, whose median is -17.3% of revenue [D844][D845].
Debt rose 138% to $4.10 billion, mainly from $1.5 billion of notes issued in March 2025 [D508][D475][P6].
Buybacks of $1.32 billion were 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 0.1% [D478][D479][D506].
Revenue fell 3.9% in FY2023, the only decline in the window, on weak PC demand and inventory correction [D370][P35].
Total debt rose 138% in FY2025 to $4.10 billion, though net cash still rose to $6.46 billion [D508][D475][D476].
The effective tax rate was -2.5% in FY2025, driven by an $853 million benefit from the release of uncertain tax positions, so the FY2025 net margin is not a clean run rate [D469][P4].
Days inventory outstanding rose to 165 days from 160, extending a climb from 106 days in FY2022 [D481][D424][D312].
If operating margin holds above the 7.2% window median in the FY2026 10-K, the FY2025 recovery is durable; a drop toward the 1.8% FY2023 level would reverse it [D795][F58].
Watch days inventory outstanding against the FY2025 level of 165 days; a further rise would signal the Data Center build is outrunning demand [D481].
Watch net cash as a share of revenue against 18.6%; a fall toward the 11.3% FY2023 level would show the debt-funded acquisitions and buybacks consuming the buffer [D477][D364].
